expect_red: a hardware pile's claims are addressed to the guards, and no surface of this page prints one

mutations.contract: `hardware_entries.claims` is a machine-readable declaration addressed to tests/claims_registry.py, and the builder carries it into every projection the viewer loads. A metric name is a key out of a test registry: it is the same class of thing as `source_ref` and `crops.json` on the reader-facing banned list, and no surface of this page may print one.
mutations.note: PLANTS A POSITIVE rather than removing a wire, because there is no wire: nothing in apps/viewer reads `results.hardware_entries` at all, so a mutation that deleted a renderer would have nothing to delete and the guard would pass over a tree in which its subject had ceased to exist. What has to be proved instead is that the scan REACHES the surfaces it walks -- the failure mode this repo has measured twice (`new RegExp(" " + name + " ")` with one backslash, matching nothing ever, and `div.worksheet__body` selecting no node on any surface the walk built). So the metric name is planted in a fixture element's NAME, which every stack-side surface renders, and the guard must find it.
